operations.before: **Independent validation:** run [[alg-krawczyk-root-certification]] on $F$ and $Z$ with $C,W,\eta$ and the supplied box budget. First its exact check $WC=I$ must succeed. For every processed subbox $Y\subseteq Z$, let $m_Y$ be its rational midpoint. The residual callback runs the validated shooting jet on $\{m_Y\}$ and returns its $F(m_Y)$ enclosure as $F_0$; the Jacobian callback runs it on $Y$ and returns its $DF(Y)$ enclosure as $J(Y)$. Both append the sound outward section-row enclosures in section mode. This uses the actual midpoint of the current Krawczyk box, even when it differs from the candidate center. A failed query or tube inclusion marks that box unresolved. All interval operations are outward under [[lem-real-interval-arithmetic-preserves-enclosure]]. Retain the complete Krawczyk output partition, including every terminal box and its status. Continue only if the overall Krawczyk status is `complete`, exactly one terminal box $Y$ has status `unique-root`, and every other terminal box has status `root-free`; if there is no such unique box, more than one, or any existence-only/unresolved box, return inconclusive. Let $X_Y$ and $\Theta_Y$ be the physical-state and period projections of the unique-root box, and include $\Lambda_Y$ in section mode. Form $Q_Y=(X_Y\times\Lambda_Y)\times\{I_{d+p}\}\times\Theta_Y$ in section mode, or $Q_Y=X_Y\times\{I_d\}\times\Theta_Y$ in fixed-parameter mode. Check $Q_Y$ is contained in the supplied augmented tube and query the same sound range provider for its augmented field enclosure. Divide the first $d$ coordinates outward by the positive interval $\Theta_Y$ to obtain an interval box containing $f(X_Y,\Lambda_Y)$ (or $f(X_Y)$ in fixed-parameter mode). Require at least one component interval to exclude zero; if inclusion, query or division fails, or no component excludes zero, return inconclusive. Finally require a successful full-box jet run on $Y$ to enclose the entire trajectory and monodromy; a failed query or tube check returns inconclusive.
operations.after: **Independent validation:** retain the exact rational candidate box $Z=\prod_{j=1}^N[a_j,b_j]$ in the declared physical variable order, where $N=d+1$ or $d+2$. If any side is degenerate, return inconclusive for validation, retaining the candidate: a box with empty ambient interior cannot pass the strict-interior inclusion required for a `unique-root` return. Degenerate boxes remain admitted inputs, and candidate-generation queries may still use their rational singleton or lower-dimensional boxes. Otherwise put $D=\operatorname{diag}(b_j-a_j)$, $T(u)=a+Du$, $B=[0,1]^N$ and $\widehat F(u)=F(T(u))$. Use the supplied open convex shooting domain containing $Z$, where the exact residual is $C^1$; failure to certify that domain returns inconclusive. The chart has an open convex preimage domain, and $D\widehat F(u)=DF(T(u))D$, by [[lem-rational-box-affine-chart-and-dyadic-enclosure]]. Run [[alg-krawczyk-root-certification]] on $\widehat F$ and the finite dyadic box $B$, using the supplied dyadic $C$, rational $W$, box budget and normalized minimum width $\widehat\eta=\eta/\max_j(b_j-a_j)>0$. Here $C$ is used as a preconditioner for this normalized residual; no approximate-inverse quality was assumed of it. The witness check remains the exact check $WC=I$. A normalized terminal box of maximum width at most $\widehat\eta$ has physical image of maximum width at most $\eta$; the budget still bounds all processed boxes. For every processed dyadic subbox $A\subseteq B$, let $m_A$ be its dyadic midpoint and set $Y=T(A)$ and $m_Y=T(m_A)$, the exact rational physical midpoint. The residual callback runs the validated shooting jet on $\{m_Y\}$ and appends the section-row enclosure when present. The Jacobian callback runs it on the rational box $Y$, appends the physical affine section row when present, and multiplies column $j$ of this physical Jacobian enclosure by $D_{jj}$. Exact rational endpoint operations followed by outward dyadic hull conversion give finite dyadic enclosures $F_0\supseteq\widehat F(m_A)$ and $\widehat J(A)\supseteq D\widehat F(A)$. A failed conversion or overflow marks $A$ unresolved; it is never supplied as a finite interval. This uses the actual midpoint of the current normalized box, whose image is the actual midpoint of $Y$, even when it differs from the candidate center. A failed query or tube inclusion marks that box unresolved. Normalized Krawczyk interval operations are outward under [[lem-real-interval-arithmetic-preserves-enclosure]]. Retain the complete normalized Krawczyk output partition, including every terminal box and its status, and its exact physical image partition under $T$. Status labels on physical images mean the corresponding root conclusions transferred by the affine bijection, not a Krawczyk computation with an unscaled physical Jacobian. Continue only if the overall Krawczyk status is `complete`, exactly one normalized terminal box $A_Y$ has status `unique-root`, and every other terminal box has status `root-free`; if there is no such unique box, more than one, or any existence-only/unresolved box, return inconclusive. Set $Y=T(A_Y)$. Let $X_Y$ and $\Theta_Y$ be the physical-state and period projections of this rational unique-root image box, and include $\Lambda_Y$ in section mode. Form $Q_Y=(X_Y\times\Lambda_Y)\times\{I_{d+p}\}\times\Theta_Y$ in section mode, or $Q_Y=X_Y\times\{I_d\}\times\Theta_Y$ in fixed-parameter mode. Check $Q_Y$ is contained in the supplied augmented tube and query the same sound range provider for its augmented field enclosure. Divide the first $d$ coordinates by the positive interval $\Theta_Y$ with exact rational endpoint arithmetic to obtain an interval box containing $f(X_Y,\Lambda_Y)$ (or $f(X_Y)$ in fixed-parameter mode). Require at least one component interval to exclude zero; if inclusion, query or division fails, or no component excludes zero, return inconclusive. Finally require a successful full-box jet run on $Y$ to enclose the entire trajectory and monodromy; a failed query or tube check returns inconclusive.

At a certified root, a tangent routine must certify a unit vector in $\ker DF$ and a rank-$d+1$ condition. The predictor is advanced along that tangent. The periodic procedure [[alg-validated-periodic-orbit-corrector]] in section mode supplies a separate Krawczyk certificate for the square shooting/section residual. Forward its complete finite input package: the candidate mode and any required differentiable pointwise/segment evaluators (or choose its enclosure-guided mode), rational initial candidate, arbitrary rational physical validation box and its open convex shooting domain, nonzero rational phase covector and rational reference point, validated-jet step counts and arithmetic caps, dyadic preconditioner and exact rational inverse witness for its normalized residual, physical minimum box width, and box/update budgets. It uses its affine dyadic unit-box chart for positive side lengths, retains the exact physical box and complete mapped partition, and returns inconclusive for validation on degenerate boxes while retaining their candidate use. For possibly nonrational tangent/predictor data, forward certified outward rational enclosures of the affine section row and its derivative; unavailable bounds return inconclusive. For every jet query reorder physical $(x,T,\mu)$ to the jet's $(x,\mu,T)$ coordinates, and return its Jacobian columns to $(x,T,\mu)$ before appending a section row. Preserve this rule in candidate, Krawczyk and continuation-evaluator calls.

Run [[alg-pseudo-arclength-continuation-with-certified-local-corrector]] using its actual exact-evaluation or bounded-error branch and its own certified Euclidean root balls. A periodic Krawczyk box alone is not its ball certificate. Use the generic exact-evaluation branch only with separately supplied exact physical point-evaluation data; interval jet enclosures alone use the bounded-error branch. The local inverse and chart suppliers remain [[lem-phase-bordered-shooting-jacobian-invertibility]] and [[thm-pseudo-arclength-local-newton-correction]], with every generic tangent, previous-normal, chart-angle, predictor-offset and finite-budget check retained. Supply the following finite-return evaluator and ball-certificate interfaces; an unavailable input returns the generic declared failure rather than an accepted step.

**Physical evaluator bridge.** At each exact queried point $y=(x,T,\mu)$, obtain a certified finite rational box containing $y$ within the shooting domain and the declared physical continuation tube; use its singleton when $y$ is rational. Every augmented range-provider tube inclusion required by the jet is checked separately in its own augmented coordinates. A nonrational query requires supplied certified coordinate enclosures, not substitution of a nearby rational point. Run the validated jet on that physical box with the stated coordinate/column permutation. Its residual and physical Jacobian intervals enclose $F(y)$ and $DF(y)$. Coordinatewise rational midpoints and the sums of the coordinate/entry radii give the generic evaluator's certified Euclidean residual error and operator-Jacobian error by [[lem-rational-box-affine-chart-and-dyadic-enclosure]]. For its current affine section form the square residual $\mathcal G(y)=(F(y),\tau_k^T(y-z_p))$ and its physical Jacobian, appending sound interval enclosures of the affine row and its constant term; include all row uncertainty in the square midpoint/error data $\widehat g,\widehat A,\epsilon_g,\epsilon_J$. These are derivatives in physical coordinates, not the normalized Krawczyk columns $DF\,D$. If only normalized data are retained, undo their known positive diagonal chart exactly and enclose the physical columns before forming these bounds. Missing finite point/row/error enclosures returns `root-certificate-inconclusive`; a certified domain/tube exit keeps the generic `tube-exit` status.

**Required Euclidean ball certificate.** At a generic candidate $y$, the callback supplies $R>0$, verifies that the whole $\overline B_2(y,R)$ lies in the declared smooth shooting domain, physical continuation tube and current isolating chart neighborhood $V_k$, and supplies a sound finite $L\ge0$ with $\|D\mathcal G(u)-D\mathcal G(v)\|_{\rm op}\le L\|u-v\|_2$ throughout that ball. This whole-ball bound is additional certified input, for example from a separately justified second-derivative bound on a covering tube. It is not inferred from first-derivative intervals, Krawczyk inclusion or the mere existence of a $C^2$ field. The callback supplies an exact rational inverse witness $V$ for the rational midpoint matrix $\widehat A$, checked by both products $V\widehat A=\widehat A V=I$, or another sound inverse-bound certificate. For the exact witness take $\widehat\beta=\sum_{i,j}|V_{ij}|$. Verify the actual tests of [[thm-augmented-residual-contraction-certificate]]:
$$\widehat\beta\epsilon_J<1,\qquad \beta=\frac{\widehat\beta}{1-\widehat\beta\epsilon_J},\qquad \rho=\|\widehat g\|_2+\epsilon_g,\qquad q=\beta L R<1,\qquad \beta\rho\le(1-q)R.$$
A certified upper bound for $\|\widehat g\|_2$ may replace the norm conservatively. Only a passing ball with the full chart/angle record can be appended by the generic algorithm. Missing witness, whole-ball Lipschitz, domain, chart or error data returns `root-certificate-inconclusive`; finite arithmetic failures and all generic budget/status distinctions remain explicit. A small residual, an exhausted Newton budget or a successful periodic Krawczyk call alone cannot append a continuation ball. If both a generic ball and a physical Krawczyk box are claimed to represent the same section root, additionally certify inclusion of the entire ball in that Krawczyk unique-root image box, or provide another sound common-root certificate; otherwise retain them as separate records without claiming coincidence.

operations.before: 1.1 By [F3], the Krawczyk run covers $Z$ with one `unique-root` box $Y$ and root-free boxes otherwise. The interval residual and Jacobian enclosures on $Y$ meet [F1], so strict inclusion gives a zero in $Y$ and the separate contraction bound gives at most one there. The root-free boxes contain no zero, hence this is exactly one zero in all of $Z$. [F1, F3, given]
operations.after: 1.1 By [F3], the actual Krawczyk run applies to $\widehat F=F\circ T$ on the dyadic unit box, with normalized Jacobian enclosure for $DF(T(u))D$. Its unique normalized box $A_Y$ satisfies [F1], so strict inclusion gives a zero and the separate contraction bound gives at most one there. Every other normalized terminal box is root-free. By [F5], $T$ sends this complete partition onto $Z$ and bijects the zeros, so $Y=T(A_Y)$ contains exactly one zero of the physical residual and every other physical image box is root-free. This is exactly one zero in all of $Z$. [F1, F3, F5, given]
